pll2d7c5-d1e3514.summary: States that though obstinate in malice, the bad angels are not wholly deprived of keen sense.

pll2d7c5-d1e3517.summary: Cites Isidore: demons flourish with threefold sharpness of knowledge, by subtlety of nature, experience of time, and revelation from higher spirits.
claims: Demons know by nature, experience, and revelation.

pll2d7c5-d1e3523.summary: Cites Augustine: evil spirits are permitted to know some truths about temporal things, by subtlety of sense, experience over a long life, and revelation from holy angels at God's command; sometimes they foretell what they themselves will do.
claims: Demons know some temporal truths by permission.
They may predict their own deeds.

pl-l2d7c5.summary: Notes that though obstinate, the bad angels are not deprived of keen sense: with Isidore, demons have threefold knowledge, by subtlety of nature, long experience, and revelation from higher spirits; Augustine adds that they know some truths about temporal things and sometimes foretell what they themselves will do.
claims: Demons know by subtlety of nature, long experience, and revelation from good angels.
Demons may foretell what they themselves will do.
